sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The is an optional boss in Elden Ring. It also appears as a field boss in Elden Ring Nightreign.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: The antler-like horns of a long-lived stag continued budding long after death, over and over again, until the beast became an Ancestor Spirit. Ancestral Spirits are a phenomenon that exists beyond the purview of the Erdtree, following the principle that life sprouts from death, just as it does birth, granting power. Its horned remains are found at the southern Hallowhorn Grounds on the bank of the Siofra River, where it lies beneath the false night sky. Its large, antler-like horns sprouted small leafy plants that shone with light, infusing nearby Ancestral Followers with profound spirituality.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
- This boss is optional.
- Furled Fingers or Spirit Ashes can be summoned for this boss.
- Deals Standard and Magic damage

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown:
- 13,000 runes
- Ancestral Follower Ashes

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown:
The horned remains of this Ancestor Spirit are found at the Hallowhorn Grounds in the lower section of the Siofra River, accessible via the Siofra River Well in Limgrave. This ruined structure is situated southeast of the Siofra River Bank Site of Grace.

In order to face this boss, the player must first light **eight** beacons scattered throughout the area. Each beacon corresponds to a pillar flanking the staircase to the Hallowhorn Grounds. Once all signals are lit, the following message displays: **Power gathers somewhere in horned remains**. The horned remains will burned with blue spectral flames, and agreeing to **Touch horned remains** will grant a supernatural encounter with the spirit.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.markdown:
- HP: 4,393
- Defense: 107
- Stance: 120
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
- Cannot be parried
- Ancestor Spirit is scripted to absorb the souls of nearby animal spirits, gaining a new attack based on the aspect. It periodically die, rebirthing itself, losing the move.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: The Ancestor Spirit is able to jump up and hop while mid-air. It can produce a jet of blue spirit vapor from its mouth, both while on the ground and in the air.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Defeating this boss for the first time unlocks the "Ancestor Spirit" achievement.
- This is the weaker version of the Regal Ancestor Spirit.
- Due to their similarities in design and behavior, Torrent may be a juvenile Ancestor Spirit.

sections.markdown: - In Norse mythology, four eat among the branches of the world tree . According to the , the stags crane their necks upward to chomp at the branches. The morning dew gathers in their horns and forms the rivers of the world.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
"Homing Instinct"** is an info item and painting in Elden Ring.
Depicts a distant Minor Erdtree, framed by ancient ruins.

Leads to the Incantation Scarab headpiece.
__TOC__

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot:** Limgrave
- Acquired from interacting with the painting found inside the Artist's Shack located on a hill, past the road north of Waypoint Ruins.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Allows the Player to perceive the soul of a painter and retrieve a unique item from their location.
The location being the point of perspective depicted by the painting itself.

The soul in question can be found near an arch of Ancient Ruins by the cliffs southeast of the First Step (or northwest from the Seaside Ruins) Site of Grace.

The painter is initially invisible when viewed from a distance but will eventually reveal themselves as the player gets physically closer to them. Successfully locating the spirit will make it dissipate before leaving the Incantation Scarab headpiece for the player to pick up from the ground.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This painting's name, "Homing Instinct" is likely a reference to Scarabs instinctively abandoning their rolled clumps, in order to return to their home nest as their lives approach its end.
 - It could also reference the feeling homesickness for Leyndell and the Erdtree displayed by Godrick and his followers. Due to its depiction of a visibly distant Erdtree and said Erdtree being in close proximity to the Tower of Return, which offers the inhabitants of Limgrave a means to quickly travel to the capital, even if the location they end up in is only a small enclosed area of it.

sections.heading: Notes

- Unlike Ash of War: Gravitas, which deals entirely Magic damage, this weapon's skill mostly Physical damage with some Magic damage, with roughly the same damage ratio as the weapon itself.
- The shortest among all greatswords.
- The 2-handed charged heavy attacks of this weapon deals damage on par with that of a Colossal Sword while draining much less Stamina than any other greatsword's. 1-handed charge attacks have similar bonuses but much less of a damage increase.
 - To be precise, the 1-handed charged heavy attacks have a roughly 10% higher damage multiplier while the 2-handed charged heavy attack has a 34% damage multiplier, and both cost only 18 points of Stamina where the average stamina cost for greatswords for both is between 35 and 42 points of Stamina for the 1-handed ones and between 38 and 48 for 2-handed ones.
- Despite that being its highest Attribute requirement, its Intelligence scaling is rather subpar.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Agheel's Flame** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Dragon Communion:** Caelid
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Flying Dragon Agheel.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of flames, dealing Fire damage equal to 169% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e., 507% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits. Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonfire.
- Compared to Dragonfire, this spell deals 17% more damage but also consumes 38% more FP.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 144 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
 - Only 79 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the third strongest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 0.5% less damage than Ghostflame Breath and 10% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
 - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:
- Borealis's Mist, a weaker Magic damage version of this spell that also inflicts Frostbite
- Dragonfire, a weaker but cheaper version of this spell
- Ekzykes's Decay, a weaker Standard damage of this spell that also inflicts Scarlet Rot
- Ghostflame Breath, a slightly stronger Magic damage version of this spell that also inflicts some Frostbite
- Smarag's Glintstone Breath, a stronger Magic damage version of this spell

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 8,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook.
- Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
 - WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Calls on a red, crackling spear from above that is then slammed into the ground, hitting with Lightning Attack Power equal to 360% of Incantation Scaling in a small 0.2 meter radius, and creating a shockwave with a 3 meter radius that hits with Lightning Attack Power equal to 285% of Incantation Scaling.

From the point of impact, waves of red lightning are sent out directly ahead and behind, and to the left and right of the caster with Lightning Attack Power equal to 122% of Incantation Scaling in a 2 meter radius from the center of each wave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Casting the spell costs 29 points of Stamina.
- Deals 17 Stance damage on a direct or shockwave hit and 5 Stance damage on a wave hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- The "direct" hit and the initial area attack cannot hit the same target, though the smaller, weakest waves can hit an enemy that has already been hit if they are either quick or large enough to also be where those are.
- The "spear" is actually flung downwards, meaning it can be used to hit the ground beneath a cliff if the caster is standing on its edge.
- Casts faster than Fortissax's Lightning Spear, but is much weaker overall and per hit.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them.
- Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
 - FP cost was decreased from 30 to 25.
 - Only the direct hit had its Stamina Attack Power increased against guarding enemies, from 100 to 140.
 - Separate Stamina Attack Power values were added for guarding players: for a direct hit, it was increased from 140 to 175; for a near hit, it was increased from 100 to 125; and for a far away hit, it was increased from 60 to 75.
- Patch 1.04 included an undocumented change which reduced the FP cost of this incantation.
 - FP cost was decreased from 42 to 30.

sections.markdown: Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants

 - WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Sends out rows of bolts in all directions, hitting at regular intervals with Lightning Attack Power equal to 317% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell sends out additional bolts to extend the range slighly and increases the Attack Power of each hit to 379% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Casting the spell costs 31 points of Stamina. Charging the spell increases the cost to 40 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases this to 9 Stance damage per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 19%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 37%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies.
 - Also deals 2 Stance damage regardless of if the original Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike was charged or not.
- This is one of the game's strongest attacks, capable of dealing over ten thousand damage to larger bosses such as the Dragonlord or the God-Devouring Serpent, even if they are resistant to Lightning, but even smaller, human-sized enemies will take heavy damage in the thousands if hit by just one or two bolts.
- This spell sometimes fails to do anything when cast under low-level roofs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Unlike other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't summon its bolts bolt from somewhere above them, instead creating them from the used Sacred Seal.
- Patch 1.04 decreased recovery time.
- Patch 1.03.3 included an undocumented changed which increased the FP cost of this incantation.
 - FP cost was increased from 27 to 36.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Alexander, Warrior Jar** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Alexander is a living jar who travels the Lands Between, honing his strength to become a great warrior. Alexander was created to be a warrior vessel, and the remains of many great warriors reside within him. He originally came from Jarburg, a hidden village of living jars in Liurnia of the Lakes; however, he vowed never to return, claiming that "the path of champions must be trod alone".

On his journey to become a grand champion, he seeks out Redmane Castle in Caelid, following rumours of a festival of combat. On his way to the festival, he crosses paths with the Tarnished multiple times, often requiring their assistance to get out of unfortunate situations such as being stuck in potholes.

Alexander finally participates in the Radahn Festival, a brawl between several champions and Starscourge Radahn. Alexander survives the ordeal, however, he suffers damage to his body and is forced to hide for the remainder of the battle. Undeterred, he replenishes himself with the bodies of mighty warriors littering the battlefield, vowing to grow even stronger.

Next, Alexander travels to Mt. Gelmir, hoping to temper his body in the sea of fire, such that it would never crack again. Finding the lava to be lukewarm and insufficient to strengthen his vessel, he sets his sights upon the Mountaintops of the Giants, seeking out the flame of ruin.

Alexander travels to the mountaintops, where he witnesses the Tarnished's fight with the Fire Giant. He then finds himself in Farum Azula, where he encounters the Tarnished for a final time. Impressed by his companion's feats of strength, he requests a duel. The Tarnished emerges victorious and Alexander accepts his defeat, asking the Tarnished to take his innards with his final words.

The Tarnished may present these innards to Alexander's nephew, the Jar-Bairn, who vows to become strong like his uncle Alexander.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Altus Plateau** is a region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The **Altus Plateau** is a northwestern region of the Lands Between. It is a region of great significance, for it is here that the Erdtree can be found, as well as Leyndell, the royal capital of Queen Marika. Altus borders Liurnia of the Lakes to the south, and the Forbidden Lands which lead to the Mountaintops of the Giants to the east. Due to its high elevation, Altus is connected to its neighbouring regions primarily through two lifts; the Grand Lift of Dectus to the south and the Grand Lift of Rold to the east. There is another, more dangerous path to Liurnia that goes through the mountains separating the two regions.

Altus is a lush and verdant land, once over-flowing with the bounty of the Erdtree itself. Most of the vegetation that grows in Altus is tinged with the gold of the Erdtree, and flowers that grow on the plateau are prized reagents by Perfumers. The people of the plateau believed that those born at the foot of the Erdtree, like themselves, were blessed. While still beautiful, the land is marred by scars from the Shattering, left over from the many battles waged here. The land is dotted by ruined battlefields and soldier's camps.

The western parts of Altus are mountainous and dominated by the volcanic Mt. Gelmir. At the top of the mountain lies the Volcano Manor, home to the demigod Praetor Rykard. At the foot of the mountain lies bubbling geysers as well as a village of Demihumans.

In the north of Altus, through a deep canyon, lies the Shaded Castle, ancient manor of the Marais family who served as both executioners and castellans of the Shaded Castle for generations. The castle lies in disrepair, haunted by Wraith-Callers and Revenants, and with most of its courtyard sinking into a poison swamp.

The eastern parts of Altus are dominated by Leyndell, Queen Marika's royal capital, built at the foot of the Erdtree. Two primary paths lead into the capital grounds; one from the southwest and one from the northwest. The southwestern path is the main road, a well-maintained and well-guarded highway gloriously decorated with statues of Queen Marika's soldiers. The capital grounds are defended by double ramparts. Within the outer wall, to the northeast, lies a Minor Erdtree. Just outside the outer wall, on an outcropping north of the southwestern highway, lies the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave, final resting place of a hero who fought against the Giants.

The inner wall of the capital is surrounded by a moat, which appears to have mostly dried out, as its waters are now shallow. Within the inner walls, the Royal Capital is bounded by a lake, which serves as yet another layer of protection. The capital is ruled by the Demigod Morgott, known also as the Veiled Monarch.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ancient Dragon Lansseax** is an optional boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background

Her most beloved knight was Vyke the Dragonspear, a Tarnished knight of the Roundtable Hold, who was later scorched by the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown:
Lansseax is first encountered near the Abandoned Coffin Site of Grace, ambushing the player near the entrance to Altus Plateau from the Ruin-Strewn Precipice. After sustaining enough damage, she abruptly ends the fight by flying away.

Her next encounter is on a hill southwest of the Rampartside Path Site of Grace, located in eastern Altus Plateau, where she can be defeated for good.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ainsel River** is an underground region in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
One of the two great rivers that flow beneath the Lands Between. Ainsel is said to be the grave of civilisations that flourished before the Erdtree. The eastern side of Ainsel is dominated by the Uhl Palace Ruins, characterised by their mausoleums and statues, and inhabited by the Claymen who served as priests of the ancient dynasty.

Nokstella, one of the Eternal Cities, can be found in the western portion of the subterranean space, inhabited by the Nox who were banished underground by the Greater Will long ago. Deeper still is the Lake of Rot, a putrid underground swamp littered with ancient ruins, where the essence of an Outer God was sealed. At the deepest point is the lair of Astel, a malformed star who once assailed an Eternal City and took away its sky. Beyond Astel is a lift which leads to the Moonlight Altar, provided the Dark Moon Ring has been found.

Ainsel can be accessed via the Ainsel River Well in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. The Ainsel River Main, which encompasses Nokstella, can be accessed via a sending gate in Renna's Rise, after Ranni the Witch gains possession of the Fingerslayer Blade.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - The name Ainsel, meaning My Own Self, is a fairy name from Scottish/Gaelic folklore. The name Siofra has similar origins.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader** is a boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Alecto was the ringleader of the Black Knife Assassins, the assailants responsible for the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. She was believed to be a Numen originating from an Eternal City. Alecto was said to have had close ties to Queen Marika herself.

sections.heading: Black Knives
sections.markdown:
After stealing a fragment of Destined Death, Ranni the Witch performed a dark ritual to imbue its power into mishappen blades. Alecto and her fellow assassins took the daggers, donned silent, silver scale armor, and made their way toward the Royal Capital.

Alecto masked her presence with a concealing veil as she and her co-conspirators entered Leyndell beneath the cover of darkness. When the moment was right, they carved the Cursemark of Death into Godwyn's flesh and slew his soul. Alecto's daughter, Tiche, died protecting her during their ensuing flight from the capital. Alecto herself was later captured and sealed within an Evergaol by an unknown party.

sections.heading: Boss fight
sections.markdown: She shares a moveset with the Black Knife Assassins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Alecto was likely trapped in the Ringleader's Evergaol by Ranni the Witch or War Counselor Iji.
